newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russians protest against proposed German memorial.
newsitem.headline: Russians protest against proposed German memorial.

text.p: Russian war veterans have banded together to try to stop a monument to German soldiers being erected north of Moscow, Interfax news agency said on Sunday -- the anniversary of the Nazis' 1941 invasion of the Soviet Union.

It said the war veterans held a conference to form a movement called the "Rzhev Barrier" -- a reference to a World War Two line of defence -- and were particularly upset that Soviet war memorials were being neglected.

"The aim of the conference organisers was to achieve a ban on the building of a memorial to German soldiers who died here in World War Two," Interfax reported from Tver, an ancient Russian town northwest of Moscow.

It said town and regional authorities had earlier agreed to allow the monument. It was not clear when the decision was taken nor who was funding the German memorial. Interfax did not say when the conference was held.
"The main reason (for the protest) was that memorials to Soviet soldiers in the area are in a pitiful state," Interfax reported.
The anniversary of the Soviet Union's entry into World War Two -- still known as the Great Patriotic War -- is one of the most hallowed dates in the Russian calendar.

In Moscow, a grand new monument, "The Peoples' Tragedy" by controversial sculptor Zurab Tsereteli, was being officially unveiled on Sunday. There were similar events and wreath-laying ceremonies across the country.
